links.outcome: Whether LLM self-expressed confidence predicts response accuracy on medical exam questions (AUROC)
links.effect: Chatbots expressed uniformly high confidence (90-100) yet self-rated confidence AUROC was only 0.52-0.68. Token probability AUROC was 0.71-0.87, and all models showed imperfect calibration with a trend toward overconfidence.
links.quote: However, expressed confidence failed to predict response accuracy (AUROC ranging from 0.52, 95% CI 0.50-0.53 for Phi-3-Mini to 0.68, 95% CI 0.65-0.71 for GPT-4o).

unlisted_practices: Using response token probabilities instead of verbalized self-rated confidence to gauge LLM answer reliability

screen.practice: token probability-based confidence signal vs self-reported confidence
screen.reason: Evaluates using token probabilities versus verbalized model confidence as a guardrail/uncertainty estimation practice to detect and mitigate overconfident incorrect answers.

primary.practice: token probability thresholding for uncertainty calibration
